extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in pop culture, late-night comedy, and entertainment industry news
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implied criteria for choosing, cutting, and presenting jokes on a late-night television show, plus standards for an awards acceptance that highlights confronting social injustice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walter Bernstein Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Walter Bernstein Award is given to “a Guild member who has demonstrated with creativity, grace, and bravery a willingness to confront social injustice in the face of adversity.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not an annual award; previous recipients noted (e.g., Jelani Cobb for Policing the Police, Ron Nyswaner for body of work). The page presents this phrasing as the defining standard for selecting the honoree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bravery/activism as basis for recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Writers Guild of America, East said Colbert has “put his career on the line to fight back against a threat to democracy.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as specific evidence supporting the award — i.e., willingness to risk one's career or take public stands in defense of civic values or against injustice is a substantive evaluative factor for this honor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing risk/backlash when deciding whether to perform a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Colbert declined to tell certain jokes because of anticipated audience reaction or potential responses (e.g., “That is why I didn’t tell that joke,” after the audience gasped at an Ivanka quip; “Didn’t do that one, didn’t want to get a call,” about a Melania joke).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical editorial guideline: weigh the likelihood and consequences of backlash or offense (audience gasp, calls from networks/subjects) when deciding to perform a joke. Examples given: Ivanka sexualized quip (‘Take Your Daughter to Climax Day’) and Melania/papal dress gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity in jokes about sexual misconduct/assault allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Even jokes written by staff about figures accused of misconduct may be cut or handled cautiously (example: a female writer’s joke about Louis C.K.: “Oh my God, he masturbates like a toddler poops.”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied standard: jokes referencing sexual misconduct or #MeToo-era allegations require careful consideration of tone, source (who wrote it), and potential harm; such material may be withheld from broadcast despite being pitched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging and spotlighting writing staff in acceptance remarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Colbert ended his acceptance speech by highlighting each of the 20 writers on his team and encouraging employment of them (“If you liked any of these ideas, please employ these lovely folks”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As an award-speech practice or professional standard: publicly credit the writers, name team members, and use platform to advocate for collaborators; this functions as part of professional conduct and recognition within the industry.
